correctness.rationale: For the truncated right circular cone, every admissible plane through the two axial witness points is an axial plane and hence gives the same isosceles-triangle section up to rotation. The radial length has two explicit branches whose transition values agree, so differentiation has no hidden moving-boundary term. Exact rational interval arithmetic proves J'(23/35)<0 and K'(33/50)>0. The strict-concavity theorem of Herburt--Moszynska--Peradzynski applies to the simple radial integral in dimensions two and three, and the tangent inequality for concave differentiable functions converts the local signs into the required opposite two-point comparisons.

value.rationale: The finding gives a strict explicit counterexample to a named archive-era convex-geometry problem. The example is a canonical right circular cone rather than an engineered high-complexity body, and the proof identifies the underlying mechanism: planar sections and the ambient three-dimensional body integrate the same radial profile with different angular weights, allowing their concave trends to disagree.
